transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes (recording length)
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Bluewave CTO), Alan Rivers (Bluewave ML), Sana Patel (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood ran a focused Optimize walkthrough showing batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations for a Bluewave Health use case (patient triage summarization). SE walked through expected cost reductions (18-45% depending on caching hit rate and batching latency targets), tradeoffs for latency vs batching, and deployment choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Action items captured to run a 24h pilot and share quantization + cost spreadsheet.

Topics: Optimize console demo, batching strategies, prefix/KV cache, cost-model math, pilot scope, security/residency Qs

Transcript: (transcription imperfect; some names/terms may be mis-typed)
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 to 55 minutes, quick intro from Redwood, then Deep dive on Optimize — especially batching and the prefix or K-V cash approach, uh cache, sorry.
[00:26] Marta Lopez: Hi thanks, Marta here from Bluewave, I'll do the security questions later but main thing is we need to drop inference cost while keeping 95th pct latency under 400 ms for triage flows.
[00:40] Priya Rao: Great, clear. Can you confirm typical payload sizes and concurrency so we can model?
[00:47] Alan Rivers: Most requests are short: 40-120 tokens input, outputs 80-200 tokens. Peak concurrency about 120 RPS for some endpoints, but average around 20 RPS.
[01:12] Priya Rao: Perfect, that matches a lot of hospital triage workloads. We'll show two levers: batching (to reduce per-token overhead) and prefix/KV cache for repeated system prompts and clinical templates.
[01:35] Sana Patel: Quick qual — what's our tolerance for occasional additional latency if it saves cost? Team target is 95% under 400ms, 99% under 800ms. Anything above that becomes a UX risk.
[01:50] Liam Chen: That's helpful. We'll demonstrate configurations that keep 95th under your target while still getting meaningful savings. If we need lower latency we can push to Dedicated or lower batching windows.
[02:12] Priya Rao: Starting with a simplified cost model — baseline hosted call: 1.2M tokens/day at $0.0004 per token-equivalent (example rate), so baseline daily cost ~ $480. If you add batching with a 40ms coalescing window and steady state concurrency, you can reduce per-token kernel overhead by ~22% in our tests. If combined with prefix/KV cache on stable system prompts that hit 30% of calls, total cost reduction estimates go to ~35-40%.
[03:00] Alan Rivers: Wait, 40ms coalescing window — does that add to tail latency or only during spikes?
[03:10] Priya Rao: Good question. Coalescing window adds that small fixed wait for the first request in a batch. In practice with 120 RPS peaks the extra wait is amortized, we usually show 20-60ms added median depending on traffic shape. We can tune per-route; low-latency routes can disable batching.
[03:35] Marta Lopez: And the KV cache — how does it affect freshness? We have partially personalized templates.
[03:45] Priya Rao: The prefix/KV cache stores static prefix KV pairs (system prompts, canned sections) in GPU memory. For partially personalized templates you can split: static prefix in cache, variable slots appended after — we saw 30-60% hit rates on many triage systems. If personalization keys are user-ID bound you can use a hybrid: short-lived KV by session. Eviction policies are LRU-like and configurable.
[04:20] Liam Chen: I'm adding a note — some transcripts read K-V cash or K-V cache as K-V 'cash' — that's fine.
[04:28] Alan Rivers: Does caching increase memory footprint significantly on the GPU?
[04:34] Priya Rao: It does use KV memory proportional to cached prefix tokens * number of model layers. For a 20-token prefix it's small; for many large templates you need to budget. We showed a sample where 5k prefixes of avg 12 tokens used ~8GB of KV memory on the model instance. We'll attach the capacity spreadsheet.
[05:10] Sana Patel: Can you show the console and how Optimize recommends settings?
[05:20] Priya Rao: Sure, screen share: the Optimize panel — note: link shared in chat to the docs and to the Optimize runbook. On the console we have workload profiler that ingests sample traces and outputs recommended batch window, target batch sizes, and estimated cost delta across hosted vs dedicated.
[06:00] [screen share noises, some crosstalk]
[06:15] Priya Rao: Here's the 'Batching' tab — it shows request size distribution, median tokens, 90th pct, and a slider for latency SLO. If we slide to 400ms SLO it suggests batch window 40ms and target batch size ~8 on current trace; projected savings 27% versus no-batch baseline.
[07:02] Alan Rivers: The projection model — is it conservative? What assumptions?
[07:10] Priya Rao: Assumptions are documented: network RTTs, kernel per-batch overhead, KV cache hit rate (you can input observed hit rate), and average token generation speed per GPU. It also models cold-starts and rare cache misses. We calibrate per-model family using Redwood-verified perf profiles.
[07:40] Liam Chen: Quick qualifier: if you move to Dedicated, running same config often gives better predictable latency and slightly better per-token cost because we can pack more tokens per GPU allocation. That's called Dedicated capacity.
[08:05] Marta Lopez: Security — can we use prefix/KV cache with Private deployment? We need to store some templates that are PHI-adjacent.
[08:15] Priya Rao: Yes. In Private or VPC deployments the KV cache remains customer-controlled memory; keys and prefixes never leave your VPC. For hosted we offer optional contract controls and SOC 2 audit logs; for PHI we generally recommend Private or on-prem.
[08:40] Alan Rivers: Any impacts on encryption / KMS?
[08:45] Liam Chen: Nothing changes in-flight; at rest of configs and logs we integrate with customer KMS and HSM for Private. We'll attach security whitepaper.
[09:05] [10m mark — brief digression about procurement timelines]
[09:20] Marta Lopez: Timeline — we need a pilot by February end or we risk missing Q2 rollout.
[09:30] Liam Chen: We can do a two-week pilot starting after you share traces. Priya can run profiling and a pilot that plugs into our Optimize runbook.
[09:45] Priya Rao: Back to cost math — example concrete scenario from today's sample: baseline average latency 210ms, no batch cost $0.48/day in our toy rate; with batch window 40ms + 30% KV hit rate we project cost to $0.31/day — about 35% reduction. For larger volumes that multiplier scales: monthly saving for 36M tokens/month becomes ~ $6,000 -> $3,900 (rough numbers).
[10:30] Alan Rivers: Are those numbers factoring in model quantization?
[10:35] Priya Rao: Not yet — we can layer quantization (4-bit/8-bit depending on model) and expect additional 10-25% reduction in GPU memory and sometimes token-level speedups. Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per workload.
[11:05] Sara (auto-transcribe mistake: 'Sara' actually Sana): Can we see an example where batching harms quality due to context shuffling?
[11:15] Priya Rao: Good point — if your model uses request-specific external context passed as per-request key/value in the prompt we must ensure batching doesn't mix contexts; Redwood runtime pins user-level context to batch slots or uses prefix slotting to avoid cross-talk. We demo that in the sandbox.
[11:45] [12:00] Demo: show a sample trace run in the sandbox where RK caching hits 35% and we measure token latency and cost.
[12:10] Priya Rao: Note: in the console we flagged certain endpoints as 'latency critical' and 'cost sensitive'. You can apply per-route policies: e.g., route /triage -> batch window 40ms, /live-chat -> no batching.
[12:45] Alan Rivers: For the pilot we will likely route triage and summarization to the batched config and keep live consults unbatched.
[13:05] Priya Rao: Exactly. Also talk about warm KV prime: you can pre-populate KV on instance boot to avoid first-call penalties.
[13:20] Marty (typo in transcript) asks about eviction and cold starts. Priya answers eviction is per-instance and we expose metrics for cache hit/miss.
[13:50] Liam Chen: Quick demo of the cost-model CSV export. We show cost vs hit rate chart and break down into kernel, token compute, and IO.
[14:10] Priya Rao: Example: with a 50% hit rate and 60% batching efficiency, savings cross 45% on token compute; but kernel overhead still matters at small tokens.
[14:45] Alan Rivers: Ok, show me what you need for the pilot.
[14:50] Priya Rao: We'll need a 48-hour request trace in ndjson or CSV, sample prompts and expected SLOs, and your security contact for the private deployment review (if you want Private). We can mock quantization options but for the pilot we test both FP16 and 4-bit quantized runs.
[15:20] Marta Lopez: We'll get logs out by Friday. Procurement loop is short but security review may take 2 weeks.
[15:40] [16:00] Liam Chen: Noted. Now a deeper technical note on batching algorithms — Redwood uses adaptive coalescing: it tracks arrival process and dynamically adjusts window to hit median latency budget while maximizing batch size. We also do request-level priority so critical requests bypass batching.
[16:55] Priya Rao: Also important: continuous KV caching vs prefix-only. Continuous KV stores the last N tokens per session for autoregressive reuse, but it's heavier. Prefix-only is recommended for templated sections. For your clinical templates we recommend prefix-only.
[17:30] Alan Rivers: What about model fallbacks? If the optimized model variant is down can requests fall back to a larger model or hosted variant?
[17:40] Liam Chen: Yes, routing policies allow fallback to compatible models, region fallback, and cost tier fallback. You can set automatic fallback to hosted when Dedicated capacity hits a queue threshold.
[18:10] Sana Patel: Any limitations with third-party PII detectors when caching?
[18:20] Priya Rao: You can strip PII before caching via preprocessing. We also provide hooks to run redaction in pipeline before KV write. For PHI we typically recommend Private with your own redaction pipeline.
[18:50] [20m mark — discussion about SLA numbers and cost splits between token compute and infra]
[19:05] Priya Rao: The cost-model CSV separates costs: raw token compute, kernel overhead, network IO, and per-request routing overhead. For most workloads kernel overhead dominates for lots of small requests. Batching reduces kernel overhead per token.
[19:40] Alan Rivers: Can the Optimize recommendations be exported as IaC? We like to codify infra as terraform.
[19:50] Liam Chen: Yes, recommendations are output as JSON/YAML which we can convert into terraform modules for Dedicated or Private deployments.
[20:10] Priya Rao: Quick live-run: we applied batch window 40ms on a sampled trace. Observed empirical end-to-end median 245ms, 95th 420ms, cost reduction 31% vs baseline.
[20:40] Marta Lopez: 95th is slightly over our 400ms target — can we tune?
[20:45] Priya Rao: Yes — options: reduce batch window to 25ms for that route, or push triage to Dedicated 2x GPU pool for better 95th predictability. The cost delta for 25ms window is small: saves 22% vs baseline but keeps 95th ~390ms in our run.
[21:20] Alan Rivers: How do we observe cache hit rates and ops in production?
[21:30] Priya Rao: Console metrics: per-instance KV hit rate, cache size, eviction counts, and per-route batch stats. We also push tracing headers so you can correlate request IDs to cache hit/miss.
[21:55] Liam Chen: Also note, Optimize can generate alert rules for when hit rate drops below expected or when batch sizes shrink significantly.
[22:20] [23:00] Discussion — tradeoffs for different sizes of user base and warmup patterns.
[23:45] Priya Rao: For smaller user bases caching yields less benefit unless templates are shared broadly. If most prompts are unique per user, batching remains the main lever.
[24:10] Alan Rivers: For our data residency, we will need Azure region in EU. Do you support region pinning?
[24:20] Liam Chen: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning; Private deployments can be fully on-prem or in your VPC in a chosen region.
[24:40] Marta Lopez: Security Q: do you maintain audit logs for KV writes and reads?
[24:50] Priya Rao: Yes — every KV write/read is logged with masked values by default, and we can turn on full logging for Private with your KMS. Audit logs are available in console and exportable.
[25:10] [26m mark] Priya Rao: Walkthrough of the pilot plan: ingest traces -> Optimize profiler -> propose batch & KV config -> run A/B pilot in sandbox -> produce cost & latency report -> recommend Dedicated sizing or Hosted config.
[25:45] Alan Rivers: Can you show a sample A/B report?
[25:50] Priya Rao: Sharing a sample from a past customer (anonymized) — with 40ms batch + 35% KV hit they achieved 37% savings and maintained 95th at 380ms.
[26:30] Liam Chen: Recap of commercial options: hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved pools (monthly commit), Private with enterprise license. Dedicated helps with predictable latency and possibly slightly better unit economics at scale.
[27:00] Marta Lopez: Pricing ask — show an example price for Dedicated two-GPU pool.
[27:10] Liam Chen: We'll include that in follow-up. Expect a monthly commit price that's competitive; exact quote depends on model family and snapshot.
[27:35] [28:00] Demo ends, open Q&A.
[28:10] Alan Rivers: What about multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated? We want tenant isolation per customer team.
[28:20] Priya Rao: Dedicated provides capacity isolation; you can also use per-route RBAC and network segmentation in Private.
[28:40] Sana Patel: If we do quantization, do we need to retrain or is it post-training quantization?
[28:50] Priya Rao: Mostly PTQ (post-training quant) supported by Redwood; for some models we recommend calibration runs. Optimize helps pick the sweet spot between quality and perf.
[29:20] Alan Rivers: Are there quality regression alerts if change to quantized model degrades metrics?
[29:30] Liam Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates with your eval sets and will alert on regression against golden prompts.
[29:55] [32m mark — technical deep dive about kernel-level improvements and quantization impact]
[31:10] Priya Rao: Quick technical aside: we compile kernels per-model/seq-length so batching benefits are sometimes model-dependent. Some architectures get more batching benefit.
[31:45] Alan Rivers: Ok makes sense. For the pilot we'll want both quantized and vanilla FP16 runs to compare.
[31:55] Priya Rao: We'll include those. Also note warm KV prime and pre-warming instances reduce first-call tail.
[32:30] [34m mark] Breeze: (auto-mislabel) discusses storage sizing for KV — estimate included in spreadsheet.
[33:00] Priya Rao: Final part — downtime & fallback policies: we can route to a smaller hosted endpoint if Dedicated is overloaded; fallback has cost but preserves availability.
[33:30] Alan Rivers: Good. Any regulatory concerns to flag?
[33:40] Liam Chen: For PHI you'll want Private; otherwise hosted with SOC 2 + data processing addendum might suffice for de-identified data. We'll loop in legal.
[34:00] [35m mark — short pause]
[34:15] Marta Lopez: Ok, can you itemize what you'll deliver after pilot?
[34:20] Liam Chen: Deliverables: pilot report (cost/latency), recommended batch & KV config, quantization recommendation, deployment proposal (Hosted or Dedicated sizing), and an enterprise security addendum if needed.
[34:50] Priya Rao: We'll also provide an IaC export for recommended infra and dashboard alerts.
[35:10] Alan Rivers: Let's talk schedule — if logs go out Friday, pilot run next Tue-Wed?
[35:20] Liam Chen: We'll aim to start Tue and finish Thu, then deliver report the following Mon.
[35:40] [36m mark] Rapid-fire Q&A on edge cases, metrics and trace formats.
[36:55] Priya Rao: On trace format — ndjson with one request per line, fields: request_id, timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, route, model_hint. That works best.
[37:20] Alan Rivers: We'll produce that.
[37:35] Sana Patel: Can Optimize recommend batching per-route automatically or do we need manual tuning?
[37:45] Priya Rao: It can auto-suggest, but we recommend an SE review for production rollouts. Auto-suggest uses historical patterns.
[38:05] [40m mark] Discussion about expected ROI and internal stakeholder alignment.
[38:25] Marta Lopez: If we reach 40% cost reduction, it's a big win. Can you commit to those numbers?
[38:35] Liam Chen: We can commit to running a pilot and showing realistic deltas; exact percent depends on your hit rates and traffic shape. We avoid guaranteeing absolute % without pilot data.
[38:55] Priya Rao: Example conservative band: 15-30% for most templated triage workloads, up to 45% if templates are heavily reused and batching is effective.
[39:30] Alan Rivers: Good. Any blockers we should anticipate?
[39:40] Priya Rao: Main blockers: inability to share traces, procurement for Private if needed, or network egress constraints.
[39:55] [42m mark] Small tangent about model family selection — some models offer better KV locality.
[40:20] Priya Rao: We'll include model family recommendations in the report with perf profiles.
[40:45] Marta Lopez: That helps.
[41:00] [44m mark] Quick recap from Liam.
[41:10] Liam Chen: Recap — Priya will run pilot, we'll share price for Dedicated, Bluewave to send traces and sample prompts, security review to be scheduled. Deliverables include pilot report and recommendations.
[41:40] Marta Lopez: Sounds good. We'll prep logs and make time for security sync.
[41:50] Sana Patel: One more thing — can you include an annex with expected memory footprint for KV entries by prefix length?
[41:58] Priya Rao: Yes, included in the spreadsheet.
[42:10] [47m mark — minor banter and confirmations]
[43:00] Alan Rivers: We'll aim to have the logs Friday EOD.
[43:12] Liam Chen: Great, we'll follow-up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
[43:25] Priya Rao: I'll also drop the Optimize runbook link and the quantization primer in the follow-up email.
[43:40] [50m mark] Last technical clarifications — per-route alert thresholds and import of eval sets.
[44:15] Priya Rao: You can register eval sets in the console and map them to alerts; we recommend a small golden set of 50 prompts for triage quality checks.
[44:45] Marta Lopez: We'll assemble one.
[45:10] [52m mark] Short closing remarks.
[45:20] Liam Chen: Thank you all. Quick reminder of next steps in chat.
[45:30] Marta Lopez: Thanks, bye.

Meeting end.
